newsitem.title: USA: Union Switch accepts Ansaldo merger offer.
newsitem.headline: Union Switch accepts Ansaldo merger offer.

text.p: Union Switch & Signal Corp said on Wednesday it unanimously accepted an offer from its majority shareholder Ansaldo Transporti S.p.A to merge Union Switch & Signal and Ansaldo's other signalling operations into one umbrella company, Ansaldo Signal N.V.
Ansaldo Signal, pro forma for the transaction, would be the second largest signalling company in the world with combined 1995 revenues of $390 million, Union said.
It would be a Netherlands holding company, with shares trading on Nasdaq under the symbol ASIGF.O, it said.
Under terms of the deal, Union Switch shareholders would receive one share of Ansaldo Signal for each Union Switch share held, the company said.

In addition, in exchange for Ansaldo Trasporti's other signaling operations, Ansaldo Signal would issue to Ansaldo Trasporti 1.1 shares of Ansaldo Signal for each share of Ansaldo Signal issued to Union Switch holders, it said.
The deal was expected to be completed by year end, Union said. Italy's Ansaldo Trasporti owned 61.6 percent of Union Switch's outstanding stock.
Ansaldo Signal's chairman of the supervisory board would be Alberto Rosania, a first vice president, strategic finance of Finmeccanica S.p.A., the company said.

Signaling operations being contributed to Ansaldo Signal by Ansaldo Trasporti include: all of Italy's Ansaldo Segnalamento Ferroviario S.p.A, all of France's CSEE Transport S.A., 75 percent of Sweden's AT Signal Systems A.B., and 100 percent of Ansaldo Trasporti Signaling (Ireland) Ltd., an Irish limited liability company.
The proposed transactions required approval by Union Switch & Signal shareholders, the company said.
